installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Enshrouded dedicated server (Windows build, run under GE-Proton)
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
# Image to install with is 'ghcr.io/pelican-eggs/installers:debian'

## just in case someone removed the defaults.
if [[ "${STEAM_USER}" == "" ]] || [[ "${STEAM_PASS}" == "" ]]; then
    echo -e "steam user is not set.\n"
    echo -e "Using anonymous user.\n"
    STEAM_USER=anonymous
    STEAM_PASS=""
    STEAM_AUTH=""
else
    echo -e "user set to ${STEAM_USER}"
fi

## download and install steamcmd
cd /tmp
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -sSL -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz
tar -xzvf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
## The platform override goes before +login. A fresh SteamCMD can still fail its first
## app_update with "Missing configuration", so retry until the server binary exists.
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    ./steamcmd.sh $( [[ "${WINDOWS_INSTALL}" == "1" ]] && printf %s '+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows' ) +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} +app_update ${SRCDS_APPID} validate +quit
    [[ -f /mnt/server/enshrouded_server.exe ]] && break
    echo "SteamCMD attempt ${attempt} did not install enshrouded_server.exe"
done
if [[ ! -f /mnt/server/enshrouded_server.exe ]]; then
    echo "SteamCMD failed to install the Enshrouded server"
    exit 1
fi

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
## Proton's lsteamclient bridge loads this; without it the server hangs before writing a log.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## enshrouded_server.json
## The server writes its full, current settings into this file on every start, adding any
## it is missing. So the installer only seeds the keys the panel manages, with their JSON
## types, and the four standard groups. The panel sets the group options by position:
## userGroups 0-3 must stay Admin, Friend, Guest and Visitor.
CONFIG=/mnt/server/enshrouded_server.json
STANDARD_GROUPS='["Admin","Friend","Guest","Visitor"]'

## fetch the seed maintained alongside this egg.
SEED_TMP="$(mktemp)" || { echo "Failed to create a temporary file for the enshrouded_server.json seed"; exit 1; }
if ! curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$SEED_TMP" https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edbfi/pelican-eggs/refs/heads/main/games-steamcmd/enshrouded/enshrouded_server.json \
    || ! jq -e --argjson groups "$STANDARD_GROUPS" '[.userGroups[].name] == $groups' "$SEED_TMP" > /dev/null; then
    echo "Failed to download a valid enshrouded_server.json seed"
    rm -f "$SEED_TMP"
    exit 1
fi

## Random passwords until the panel writes its own on the first start.
random_password() { tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 24; }
SEED="$(mktemp)" || { echo "Failed to create a temporary file"; exit 1; }
jq --arg admin "$(random_password)" --arg friend "$(random_password)" \
    --arg guest "$(random_password)" --arg visitor "$(random_password)" \
    '.userGroups[0].password = $admin | .userGroups[1].password = $friend
    | .userGroups[2].password = $guest | .userGroups[3].password = $visitor' \
    "$SEED_TMP" > "$SEED"
rm -f "$SEED_TMP"

if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    echo "Creating enshrouded_server.json"
    cp "$SEED" "$CONFIG"
elif jq -e --argjson groups "$STANDARD_GROUPS" '[.userGroups[:4][].name] == $groups' "$CONFIG" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "Keeping the existing enshrouded_server.json"
else
    ## Legacy layout, e.g. a single "Default" group migrated from a top-level password.
    BACKUP="${CONFIG}.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).bak"
    cp "$CONFIG" "$BACKUP"
    echo "enshrouded_server.json lacks the standard user groups; backed up to ${BACKUP}"
    ## Keep its settings, tags and bans; put the standard groups first and any others after them.
    if jq --slurpfile old "$BACKUP" --argjson groups "$STANDARD_GROUPS" '
            $old[0] as $o
            | . * ($o | del(.userGroups, .password, .gamePort))
            | .userGroups += [($o.userGroups // [])[] | select(.name as $n | $groups | index($n) | not)]
        ' "$SEED" > "$CONFIG"; then
        echo "Merged the existing settings into the current layout"
    else
        echo "The existing file is not valid JSON; starting from the seed"
        cp "$SEED" "$CONFIG"
    fi
fi
rm -f "$SEED"

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: [Server] Server Name
variables.description: Name shown in the in-game server browser.

variables.name: [Server] Max Players
variables.description: Player slots (slotCount). The game allows 1 to 16.

variables.name: [Server] Difficulty Preset
variables.description: gameSettingsPreset. Default, Relaxed, Hard or Survival use the built-in values; Custom applies the gameSettings block in enshrouded_server.json.

variables.name: [Admin] Password
variables.description: Password for the Admin group (userGroups[0].password). Players receive this group's configured permissions when they join with this password.

variables.name: [Admin] Kick / Ban Players
variables.description: Allow kicking and banning players. Sets userGroups[0].canKickBan.

variables.name: [Admin] Access Inventories
variables.description: Allow using chests, containers and workstations. Sets userGroups[0].canAccessInventories.
